articles.title: In 2013, British national Sarah Groves was found dead with 43 wounds on Kashmir houseboat; 13 years later court has ordered fresh psychiatric assessment of Dutch man accused of her murder
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: A team of doctors is set to re-examine Dutch citizen Richard de Wit, accused of murdering British national Sarah Groves in New Beauty houseboat
articles.body: SRINAGAR: A team of doctors is set to re-examine Dutch citizen Richard de Wit, accused of murdering British national Sarah Groves in New Beauty houseboat in Dal Lake in 2013, at Srinagar’s Central Jail on Thursday to assess whether his psychiatric and general medical condition allows him to stand trial.“The present case has remained pending for a considerable period and the progress of the trial has from time to time been impeded due to the reported medical, particularly psychiatric, condition of the accused,” the court of the 2nd Additional Sessions Judge said.The court said that reports received from jail authorities disclosed that the accused has not been cooperating with psychiatric consultations, hospitalisation, medical examinations and the treatment advised by medical professionals.It was also reported that the accused had refused to cooperate with efforts to take him from the jail to an outside medical facility for examination and treatment.“The reported non-cooperation has, therefore, presented a practical impediment to securing the medical assessment necessary for determining the further course of the proceedings,” the court said. The court also said the question requiring consideration was whether, in view of his present psychiatric and general medical condition, the accused was capable of understanding the nature of the judicial proceedings, communicating meaningfully with his counsel and participating in the trial in accordance with law.Such a determination, it said, could not be made solely on the basis of a judicial impression or reports of non-cooperation, but required an objective and independent assessment by qualified medical professionals. The court then directed the Medical Superintendent, government psychiatric diseases hospital, Srinagar, to constitute a competent team of doctors for the fresh and comprehensive examination of the accused in the Central Jail, Srinagar, on October 29 2026.The court said the MS government psychiatric diseases hospital and the superintendent, central jail, Srinagar, should coordinate the necessary arrangements to ensure the presence of the medical team at the specified time. The court said the team should have a specialist in psychiatry, a specialist in general medicine, and specialist or medical practitioner as may be considered necessary in view of the reported condition of the accused,” the Court said, adding the examination within the jail should be conducted in an appropriate setting, with due regard to the dignity, safety and medical interests of the accused.On April 6, 2013, 24-year-old Sarah Groves was found dead inside her room in the New Beauty houseboat in Dal Lake in Srinagar. In the case of murder of Sarah Groves, the police arrested Richard de Wit, that time 43, around 77 kms, from the scene of murder, on the same day, a few hours after the murder. Richard De Wit, son of Handrik Pietor De Wit of Ridder Kerk Netherlands, according to the police chargesheet, was trying to move out from the valley, some hours after committing the murder. He was arrested in the town of Qazigund, around 70 km south of Srinagar. He was in wet clothes and without shoes. He was carrying his passport.Miss Groves had travelled to Srinagar in February that year as she was intending to stay in the valley for some time. De Wit arrived at the guesthouse on April 3, and was staying at the cabin next to Miss Groves. They were the only two tourists staying on the boat. De-Wit, according to the police, had allegedly stabbed Sarah to death. She had around 43 wounds on her body. Afadul Mujtaba, who was then Deputy Inspector General (DIG) police, Central Kashmir range, was first to question the accused had described him “having paranoia and had thought that the Dutch intelligence agencies were after him for his anti-government political beliefs and he had murdered Sarah presuming her as Dutch agent.”Stay updated with the latest Srinagar news. articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: 2 dead, over 50 trains, several flights cancelled; Andhra, Odisha worst-hit
articles.summary: VIJAYAWADA: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early on Wednesday, killing two people in separate electrocution incidents, uprooting hundreds
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early on Wednesday, killing two people in separate electrocution incidents, uprooting hundreds of trees and electric poles and damaging roads.Flight operations were also disrupted at airports across coastal Andhra Pradesh, with several services cancelled or suspended due to adverse weather.The very severe cyclonic storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between 2 am and 8 am before weakening into a severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.The cyclone crossed the coast southwest of Yanam, near latitude 16.450 N and longitude 81.90 E, about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40 km southwest of Yanam and 60 km southwest of Kakinada, according to the IMD.Several locations in coastal districts recorded heavy rainfall exceeding 200 mm, while strong winds uprooted trees and power poles, blocked roads and disrupted electricity supply.According to news agency PTI, two people, including a 55-year-old woman, died of electrocution in separate incidents. A 53-year-old man died in Visakhapatnam district on Tuesday night after coming into contact with a live wire that had snapped over an agricultural field channel.In Yellamanchili town in Anakapalli district, a woman died on Wednesday morning after accidentally stepping on an exposed live wire outside her home, police said.Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the situation on Wednesday morning during a teleconference with 32,000 personnel, including district collectors, and directed officials to restore normalcy at the earliest while minimising property damage.He instructed officials to clear roads blocked by fallen trees within two hours and remove trees obstructing national highways immediately. Electricity supply should be restored once strong winds subside, he said.Naidu also directed officials to ensure adequate food, drinking water and medical facilities at cyclone shelters, protect horticultural crops, prevent water from entering agricultural fields and take measures to prevent breaches in tanks and canals.For this cyclone, the Air Force assisted in transporting teams; yesterday, they airlifted four teams. In terms of preparedness, our priority is to ensure the safety of vulnerable groups—the elderly, pregnant women, and children. Pregnant women, in particular, are shifted to hospitals or dispensaries in anticipation of the event. Furthermore, all boats are either brought back to the shore and anchored securely or moved to a safe area...People living in low-lying areas, identified based on historical records, are also moved to safer locations. Through our warning system, local agencies and authorities conduct outreach at the community level to raise awareness, ensuring that necessary safety precautions are takenHe asked officials to prepare preliminary estimates of crop damage and keep National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel on standby.Trees uprooted, roads damagedKakinada Superintendent of Police G Bindu Madhav said the district had been significantly affected by the storm."Cyclone Arnab had significantly affected the district, uprooting a few hundred trees and fewer than 100 electric poles. However, no major damage has been reported and rainfall subsided after 1 am," he said.People evacuated to relief camps remained there until 1 am on Wednesday as strong winds continued, he added. The Uppada coastal road had been completely washed away, though rainfall in the district was relatively low and gusty winds caused most of the damage.In Alluri Sitaramaraju district, trees and electric poles were uprooted and some roads inundated. District SP Amit Bardar said no deaths or major damage to infrastructure, houses or livestock had been reported as of 9 am."No loss of life or major damage to infrastructure, houses or livestock has been reported so far. We are monitoring the situation closely as water levels may rise due to continued rainfall," Bardar told PTI.An old bridge in Tadiguda village of Anantagiri mandal was washed away, isolating a hamlet. Alternative arrangements were being made and restoration work was underway, he said.In Konaseema district, gusty winds reaching up to 130 kmph uprooted trees and electric poles late on Tuesday night, district police chief Rahul Meena said. No casualties or property damage had been reported.More than 10,000 people had been evacuated from low-lying areas and moved to shelters, according to preliminary information. Around 495 cyclone shelters and temporary relief centres had been set up, Meena said.Additional Andhra Pradesh Special Police platoons were deployed for clearance operations, with personnel from various departments working to restore normalcy by evening. Electricity supply was expected to be restored within a few hours, while major highways were expected to be cleared within two to three hours.In Visakhapatnam district, around 400 trees had fallen, District Collector M Abhishikth Kishore said. Roads and Buildings department and Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation teams were carrying out clearance operations, with most roads already reopened to traffic."About 100 families are currently staying at two relief centres while few others have returned to their homes. No inundation has been reported anywhere in the district," Kishore told PTI.Anakapalli district SP Tuhin Sinha said no major issues had been reported in the district.Several flights cancelledThe IMD said rainfall exceeding 200 mm was recorded at several locations in Anakapalli, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam districts between 8.30 am on October 27 and 4 am on October 28.Kannuripalem in Anakapalli recorded the highest rainfall at 261.5 mm, followed by KVBR School in Vizianagaram district at 259.74 mm and the 16th Police Battalion area in Visakhapatnam at 259.06 mm.State government officials said heavy rainfall was likely to continue on Wednesday and Thursday due to the cyclone's impact.The Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) said flights to and from coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, including Bhubaneswar, were expected to be the most affected. Hyderabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur could also see knock-on delays depending on the storm's track.Flight operations at Visakhapatnam airport had been suspended since the afternoon of October 27, while flights at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry were suspended after 7 pm that day.The Delhi-Bhogapuram-Delhi service was cancelled for October 28.Air India cancelled six flights on the Delhi-Visakhapatnam-Delhi route on October 27 and the Delhi-Vijayawada-Delhi route on October 28. Air India Express reported 13 cancellations, mostly involving Visakhapatnam flights to and from Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Vijayawada, along with the Varanasi-Bangkok and Bangkok-Visakhapatnam services.IndiGo suspended all flights at Visakhapatnam and services at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry after 7 pm on October 27. The cancellation figures were provisional.Akasa Air cancelled its Delhi-Bhogapuram and return services scheduled for October 28, while its other flights were expected to operate. Alliance Air was operating normally, with no cancellations reported so far.MoCA stressed coordination among the Airports Authority of India, Directorate General of Civil Aviation, Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, IMD, airlines, airport operators, disaster management authorities in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal, and the NDRF to ensure passenger safety.Airlines were advised to follow operational guidelines for adverse weather, inform passengers about delays and cancellations, and comply with applicable rebooking and refund rules.Passengers were advised to check flight status through airline websites, apps, helplines or SMS before leaving for the airport. They were also asked not to travel unless their flight was confirmed and to allow extra time for their journey.57 trains cancelled, 15 rescheduledSouth Coast Railway (SCoR) has cancelled 57 trains and rescheduled 15 others as a precautionary measure in view of severe Cyclone Arnab, disrupting several key services, including Vande Bharat, Ratnachal, UDAY, Garib Rath, Godavari and Falaknuma Express trains.Railway authorities said the cancellations and rescheduling were undertaken to ensure passenger safety and facilitate smooth train operations amid adverse weather conditions expected along the Andhra Pradesh coast.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: Couple receives an anonymous letter from the last surviving family member of their 130-year-old home; it opened secret passages to a hidden liquor cabinet with antique bottles, and a creepy attic behind a mysterious door
articles.summary: Most of us open our mailbox and letters without a second thought, with bills, flyers, and the occasional birthday card, or receiving deliverables ordered
articles.body: Most of us open our mailbox and letters without a second thought, with bills, flyers, and the occasional birthday card, or receiving deliverables ordered online*.But what if an anonymous letter arrives that suddenly opens up hidden details and secret rooms of the 130-year-old house that you just bought and live in?A similar incident happened with Courtney and Matt, who received an envelope addressed to the “purchaser.” The letter had travelled all the way from Canada and came from someone who clearly knew a great deal about their home, and it turned out that their 130-year-old house had been keeping secrets!The writer described themselves as the “last surviving member” of the family that once owned the estate. Not a stranger, not a salesperson, but someone with a lifetime of history tied to those very walls. And they had decided the new owners deserved to know what the house had never told them.Let’s dig in to find out what exactly happened.Last surviving member of a 130-year-old house reveals a a secret liquor cabinet and a "creepy" atticCourtney and Matt, a married couple who share their old-house adventures on TikTok with username @living_in_history, went viral after showing off a very unusual piece of mail. According to their TikTok video posted previously, they received a letter at their nearly 130-year-old Victorian-style house addressed simply to the "purchaser."They revealed that the sender lived in Canada and described themselves as the last surviving member of the Madison family, who once owned the house. The letter said, “It says, ‘Let me introduce myself. I am the last surviving member of the Madison family who once owned the house, and I grew up in it,’” additionally, the sender wrote, “‘I would like to … tell you about the secret rooms and a few things you may not have been told when you bought the house.’”However, the couple did not reveal where exactly the house was and shared little about the Madison family. In a separate video mentioned by the Post, the couple said they bought the house from a historical society.From hidden wine cabinet to an attic: What all did the receivers find?The first stop was the front parlor. According to the video, they pulled back a sliding mirrored panel and found a hidden cabinet packed with old bottles of alcohol. It was a concealed treasure trove with a vintage collection including French rosé from 1970 and cabernet sauvignon from 1989, along with aged bourbon, beer, and cream sherry.Next, the letter pointed to a spot in the bathroom, directly opposite the door in the wall. Courtney called it the scariest room in the house, but it was not a room at all. Dexerto describes it as a small crawl space: “My guess is there probably used to be some kind of room up here,” said Courtney, “but really, it’s just a creepy attic space.”Apart from this, there was also a locked door opposite the toilet that led to a much bigger surprise, which was a large trunk room. Courtney told viewers, “We’re going to try and figure out how to use this space, but right now it’s just kind of a cool, cool room.”The letter gives the story its heart and shows how a profound thought by someone who grew up in the house wanted its new owners to know it properly, and even till the end, the couple did not find out who sent the letter.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Worker killed in Balasore filling station blast, protests erupt
articles.summary: Balasore petrol pump blast: worker killed when old underground fuel tank exploded during gas-cutting; protests, vandalism, and police probe underway.
articles.body: Balasore: A worker was killed in an explosion while an old underground fuel tank was being cut with a gas cutter at a filling station in Baligohiri under Nilagiri police limits in Balasore district on Wednesday. The incident triggered tension at the petrol pump, with angry locals demanding justice for the deceased.The deceased was identified as Birendra Singh, alias Hua (58), of Bimuria village under Remuna block. He was working at the filling station when the explosion occurred.According to sources, a new fuel tank had been installed at the petrol pump, and work was underway to cut the old tank using a gas cutter. The tank suddenly exploded during the operation, sending its lid flying and striking Birendra. He sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.Following the incident, tension prevailed at the petrol pump as locals accused those responsible for the work of negligence. Some angry people allegedly vandalised the premises, demanding accountability for the worker’s death.Nilagiri police station IIC Gobardhan Nayak reached the spot with a police team and initiated an investigation. Police took petrol pump owner Diptikanta Mohapatra, manager Kamal Lochan Nayak and two workers engaged in the gas-cutting operation to the police station for questioning.Meanwhile, Birendra’s family members staged a protest by placing his body on the Nilagiri-Sergarh road, demanding compensation and justice. Police personnel attempted to pacify the protesters and bring the situation under control.Birendra’s brother, Jogendra Singh, alleged that negligence on the part of the company and petrol pump authorities had led to the tragedy.“Before cutting a fuel tank with a gas cutter, the authorities should have taken the necessary precautions. Even if a tank is empty, residual gas or other combustible substances may remain inside, creating a risk of an explosion. articles.title: In 2003, Alicia Keys co-founded a charity to help children affected by HIV; two decades later, it has raised $86.6 million and supports 9.3 million children, young people and families in 28 countries
articles.summary: Alicia Keys, 45, is now a mother of five (two biological children and three stepchildren).
articles.body: Alicia Keys, 45, is now a mother of five (two biological children and three stepchildren). Motherhood came to her as an adult, but the instinct to look after children was there well before that. Long before she had children of her own, she was already caring about children on the brink of neglect.Alicia Keys was just 20 when she travelled to South Africa as part of MTV’s Staying Alive campaign. During the visit, she went to clinics where pregnant women and new mothers were confronting the reality of HIV/AIDS, including the risk of passing the virus on to their babies. She also witnessed widows and children orphaned by AIDS struggling to survive. “I couldn’t turn my back on all I’d seen,” Keys told WebMD at the time. The experience inspired her to co-found Keep a Child Alive in 2003 alongside AIDS activist Leigh Blake, with the aim of helping children and families affected by HIV/AIDS access life-saving medication and essential support.Twenty years later, the non-profit charity had raised $86.6 million, worked in 28 countries and supported over 9.3 million children, young people and families.A trip that changed many livesAt 20, Keys travelled to South Africa as part of MTV’s Staying Alive campaign, which focused on HIV and AIDS. What she saw there changed her life and many others for the better. “At the time, a lot of women didn’t realize that if you are positive and you breastfeed your baby, your baby will contract it,” Keys told People in 2019. “The moms just wanted medicine to keep them alive. That was the first time as a 20-year-old that I was aware of the injustice. I thought, ‘How can something be available, but you can’t have it because you’re poor?’ I just felt like that was a death sentence. That’s what outraged me and motivated me. When I came back, I was never the same.” She couldn’t just turn her back on these children and women. She had to do something.Keep a Child AliveThat something became a non-profit organisation called Keep a Child Alive. True to its name, its mission was to keep children alive. The aim was to support children facing the most challenging circumstances. Keys built the organisation with AIDS activist Leigh Blake, who had already worked on the issue for years. Blake had helped organise a 2001 remake of Marvin Gaye’s “What’s Going On” to raise AIDS awareness, with Bono as co-executive producer, and had funded a clinic in Kenya. Keep a Child Alive launched in 2003 with a simple aim: to get life-saving AIDS medication to children and families who could not afford it. Blake took the lead on the medical and fundraising side, while Keys became the public face. Keys’ contribution over the years has been steady. Its annual fundraiser, the Black Ball, has been a regular fixture on New York’s calendar.The non-profit has 41 partners, according to the organisation. The Hell’s Kitchen partnership was one of the group’s more visible recent efforts. Starting in April 2024, the production and ticketing partner TodayTix Group pledged $1 from every ticket sold for the Broadway run. In October, the show announced that it had donated $1 million, including matching gifts. The charity said that sum would reach 18,250 children across eight countries. A later statement put the total at more than $1.5 million.“I have taken such pride in being a co-founder of Keep a Child Alive since its creation over 20 years ago and all the lives we have been able to touch and all that we have been able to accomplish so far. Hell's Kitchen is about a 17-year-old girl trying to find her way in NYC. Both Hell's Kitchen and Keep a Child Alive believe that every child in the world should have the opportunity to thrive. I feel immense gratitude that we can partner, with equal passion, to create an even greater force for change,” Alicia Keys said in a statement released on the non-profit’s website.Keys started the organisation to get antiretroviral drugs to children who had no other route to treatment. It was an emergency effort to reach families in South Africa, Uganda, India, Kenya and Rwanda. Over time, the mission widened to cover health, education and human rights, though HIV remains at its centre.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Not blind but not the same: Kids still bear brunt of carbide guns
articles.summary: BHOPAL: At 12, Senu is back in school, but his dream of studying at Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya remains out of reach.
articles.body: BHOPAL: At 12, Senu is back in school, but his dream of studying at Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya remains out of reach. A year after a carbide gun injured his right eye during Dhanteras festivities in Ashta, the farmer's son still wears protective glasses outdoors and occasionally experiences swelling.The ordeal may have occurred last year but it has cast a pall of gloom over his future and that of several kids across MP., for whom the threat of carbide guns is a reality they have to contend with every day.Carbide guns were sold openly by the roadside in Bhopal, Gwalior and other cities, promoted by viral reels and early warning signs- like FIRs on cases and a 2023 ICMR report- had went unheeded across the state until it was too late. Senu and kids like him are still bearing the brunt of such delays in action.Senu had prepared for the entrance examination for Class VI at the residential school, buying an application form for Rs 500 and preparation books worth Rs 700. But the injury and the struggle to arrange money for specialised treatment disrupted his preparations. Now studying in Class VI at a regular school, he hopes for another chance, with his father seeking a govt exception to the admission process. For Jitendra Verma, a farmer from Khamkheda Jatra, around 14 km from Ashta, the injury brought a financial burden alongside his son's medical ordeal. He says he spent nearly Rs 15,000 on treatment in Bhopal, borrowing money after initially seeking care locally. A year later, the family has received no compensation, despite possessing an Ayushman Bharat card, he says. Already burdened by other loans, Jitendra continues to seek govt assistance.Senu's case reflects the longer-term consequences of carbide gun injuries reported during Diwali festivities in Madhya Pradesh. An ophthalmologist at Gandhi Medical College, Bhopal, Dr Aditi Dubey, who treated such patients, says around eight to ten children have suffered lasting effects on their vision. Although these kids are not necessarily blind, impaired eyesight could affect their eligibility for certain jobs and entrance exams that require 6/6 vision, depending on the applicable medical standards.A year on, Senu continues his education, but the injury has left his family grappling with unanswered questions over compensation and his educational future. articles.title: Netanyahu and rival face tough battle for power with most votes counted
articles.summary: Neither side has an obvious path forward as the Israeli election result heads toward a deadlock. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• No clear winner : With most votes counted, Israel is facing political deadlock , with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival, ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot, within reach of a governing majority in Israel’s parliament, the Knesset.

• Latest numbers: Recent projections have Netanyahu’s bloc taking 53 seats, a drop from the 68-seat coalition he led in the outgoing Knesset. The opposition bloc is set to take 48 seats, while Arab parties are projected to win a record 19 seats.

• Complicated route: The opposition bloc and Arab parties have a clear majority, but some of Eisenkot’s allies oppose working with Arab parties. Several scenarios are possible, while Israel’s president called on parties to keep an “open mind” to avoid more elections.

Election officials are in the final stretches of the vote count and with more than 85% of the ballots in, Israel seems set for a political deadlock . Complete results are expected on Thursday , but it is now certain that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival, ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot , will secure the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat parliament, the Knesset.

Netanyahu defiant despite losses: The incumbent prime minister said his bloc had the support of a “decisive majority among the Zionist and Jewish public.” The right-wing grouping is set to take 53 seats , a loss of 15 compared to the last election in 2022. Still, Netanyahu’s Likud party is expected to be the biggest in the parliament.

No clear path for the challenger: Eisenkot’s opposition bloc is now projected to get 48 seats in the Knesset, 13 short of the majority. To govern, he would likely need to rely on the support of Israel’s Arab parties , a long-standing political taboo among most Jewish parties. Still, Eisenkot framed his result as a win, saying “the public has voted for change.”

Arab parties surge: The two parties representing Arab citizens of Israel, Ra’am and the Joint List , are set to secure about 19 seats – the highest ever. Arab voters make up about 20% of the Israeli electorate, but have traditionally voted at lower rates than Jewish Israelis. This time around, they showed up in huge numbers.

Attempt to delegitimize: Netanyahu’s Likud party has tried to delegitimize the Arab vote, and on Wednesday accused the two parties of “stealing” the election. Election integrity monitoring was in place at all polling stations throughout voting hours, officials said. The Central Elections Committee’s systems received approximately 10,000 reports for review concerning suspected election integrity incidents and had said that all cases had been addressed and closed. On Wednesday evening, the committee issued a new statement saying it had received Likud’s inquiry, and was examining it.

Record turnout: Nearly 5.7 million voters cast their ballot out of approximately 7.3 million eligible voters on Election Day – meaning a turnout of 77.7%, the highest percentage since 1999, according to the Central Elections Committee.

What’s next: Once the count is finalized, the political horse trading will begin. The president will talk to the elected parties and then ask the person who has the best chance of building a viable coalition to form a government. They’d have six weeks to cobble together a majority and if they fail, the runner-up will be invited to try. If they can’t do it either, and if the Knesset cannot put forth another candidate, Israel could hold elections all over again.

It’s 5:45 p.m. in Jerusalem and with just over 85% of the ballots counted, these are the latest projections of how the 120 seats in the Knesset might be divided based on the votes tallied so far:

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc is set to take 53 seats, eight short of a majority and 15 fewer than it has in the outgoing parliament. Netanyahu’s party is the biggest one of the group, projected to secure 26 seats.

The opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, now has 48 seats. Eisenkot’s party Yashar is set to get 21 seats.

Arab parties – Ra’am and the Joint List – have 19 seats.

The last batch of ballots to be counted will be the 430,000 to 480,000 “double envelopes” which are used by voters who exempt from having to vote in their place of residents. These include votes by soldiers, diplomats, patients in hospitals, prisoners and evacuees.

Ever since polls closed on Tuesday night, Israel’s Central Elections Committee (CEC) has been counting the votes and updating the results. But the process is not instantaneous, and there are still hours of work ahead.

By Wednesday evening, the committee is expected to finish counting all of the election day ballots that were submitted at polling places. When that process wraps up, the focus turns to the double envelope ballots. A group of voters — soldiers, prisoners, hospital patients and staff, diplomats abroad and voters with disabilities — cast their ballot inside a double envelope.

These voters place their anonymous vote in an inner envelope sealed inside an outer envelope with their personal details. The double envelopes are transported to the CEC, where staff check each outer envelope against the registered polling stations to verify that a voter didn’t vote twice. Only then are the inner envelopes separated and counted.

The CEC estimated that there could be between 430,000 and 480,000 double envelopes to count, a process that will take time. Only when that process concludes — potentially sometime Thursday morning or afternoon — will we know the final results of Israel’s election. But even that only tells us the size of the parties. Whether there is an outright winner will still depend on coalition building and political negotiations.

With most votes counted, Israel’s election has produced no clear winner, setting up weeks - and possibly months - of political uncertainty. Several outcomes and scenarios may come into play.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc has lost the majority it held in the outgoing parliament. With about 53 seats projected, it falls short of the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government in the 120-seat Knesset.

Netanyahu could try to recruit one of the opposition parties to join his government, but they all ruled out cooperation with him during campaigning. Politicians who have joined him in recent years have often found themselves significantly weakened with little substantive influence over policy. Netanyahu could also try to seek individual opposition defectors, but that would require several defections to close the gap.

The opposition, on the other hand, has won a majority in the parliament, but their path to power is crossed by ideological, national and personal divisions.

Netanyahu’s main rival Gadi Eisenkot is projected to win 21 seats, but he cannot reach the 61-seat majority without the two Arab parties, Ra’am and the Joint list, who are projected to win a record 19 seats. On Wednesday, Yair Golan, the leader of the left-wing Democrats party, called on his partners to count the Arab parties as part of the bloc, rejecting what he called Netanyahu’s “racist division between Jewish and Arab votes.”

But two of Eisenkot’s right-wing allies oppose forming a government that includes the Arab parties or a minority government that relies on their outside support.

Given the apparent deadlock, another scenario is a national unity government pairing Netanyahu’s Likud and one or more parties from the opposition, an option that would replace his current hardliner government. Both Netanyahu and the opposition leaders have ruled this out during the campaign, but it may be one of the only ways to avoid another election.

In his first public statement since polls closed, Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for political parties to have “an open mind” in order to avoid another round of elections.

After the results are certified, Herzog begins meeting with all of the political parties in order to determine which candidate has the best chance of forming a government. But if no one can succeed in forming a government, Israel automatically goes back to another round of elections, a scenario Herzog has made clear he wants to prevent.

“So I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind,” he said.

Herzog also hailed the high voter turnout as a sign of Israel’s democracy. “Yesterday’s election day was truly impressive, with the highest turnout in decades. It is a badge of honor for Israeli society, and it was remarkable to see how deep the desire for democracy is in Israel,” he said.

With counting well underway in Israel, elsewhere the country’s embassy in Belgrade found itself under what the Serbian authorities called a “terrorist attack.”

Serbia’s interior ministry said an attacker wielding two knives wounded a policeman guarding the embassy shortly after midnight local time. Despite suffering injuries to the face, the officer managed to shoot the assailant, killing him in what the ministry said was self-defense.

The ministry raised the country’s terror alert level following the incident.

Serbia’s outgoing Minister of Interior Ivica Dacic said in a statement that the attacker was as of yet unknown minor from western Serbia who “shouted ‘Allahu Akbar’ and attacked the member of gendarmerie with two ​knives.”

Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said “no embassy personnel were injured, and the mission was closed at the time of the incident.”

Israeli election officials are still counting the votes cast in yesterday’s parliamentary election. With almost 80% counted, Israel seems set for a political deadlock . Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival, ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot , have the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat parliament, the Knesset.

Netanyahu defiant despite losses: The incumbent prime minister said his bloc had the support of a “decisive majority among the Zionist and Jewish public.” The right-wing grouping is set to take 54 seats , a loss of 10 compared to the last election in 2022. Still, Netanyahu’s Likud party is expected to be the biggest in the parliament.

No clear path for the challenger: Eisenkot’s opposition bloc is now projected to get 47 seats in the Knesset, 14 short of the majority. To govern, he would likely need to rely on the support of Israel’s Arab parties , a long-standing political taboo among most Jewish parties. Still, Eisenkot framed his result as a win, saying “the public has voted for change.”

Arab parties surge: The two parties representing Arab citizens of Israel, Ra’am and the Joint List , are set to secure about 17 seats – the highest ever. Arab voters make up about 20% of the Israeli electorate, but have traditionally voted at lower rates than Jewish Israelis. This time around, they showed up in huge numbers.

What’s next: Once the count it finalized, the political horse trading will begin. The president will talk to the elected parties and then ask the person who has the best chance of building a viable coalition to form a government. They’d have six weeks to cobble together a majority and if they fail, the runner-up will be invited to try. If they can’t do it either, and if the Knesset cannot put forth another candidate, Israel could hold elections all over again.

For a country the size of New Jersey, Israel draws an outsized share of international attention and headlines. US President Donald Trump’s relationship with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – and the Iran war they launched together – is part of the reason.

Amichai Cohen, the Vice President of Research at the Israel Democracy Institute, lays out three more reasons the world is watching these elections so closely.

First, is the hope that a different government in Israel would be willing to engage more on diplomacy in the Middle East and the potential of ending conflicts in Iran, Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza. “Perhaps there are also routes for possibly reopening negotiations with the Saudis (toward normalization),” he said.

The world is also watching closely to see what will happen in the occupied West Bank . Netanyahu’s government drove a massive expansion in Israeli settlements while downplaying a surge in settler violence toward Palestinians. The UK and a dozen other countries are preparing sanctions against Israeli settlements, and that list may well expand if another Netanyahu government drives the same policy of entrenching Israel’s grip on the territory.

Finally, Cohen told CNN that Israel has been perceived internationally as a country in democratic decline. Netanyahu’s government pushed a judicial overhaul that would’ve seen a weakening of checks and balances, as well as attacks on the press.

“ The question of whether anti-populist forces will be able to reclaim democracy is an important question universally and Israel is, to a certain extent, an important part of this discussion,” Cohen said.

The father of an American-Israeli soldier killed on October 7, 2023 said he fears another Benjamin Netanyahu term as prime minister will deny families still grieving the deadliest attack in Israel’s history answers.

“It’s about how did this happen.” Ruby Chen, father of deceased soldier Itay Chen, told CNN’s Salma Abdelaziz Wednesday.

“As long as Prime Minister Netanyahu is in power, he will never create an investigation committee.”

Chen has long advocated for an investigation into how the coordinated assaults by the terrorist group were able to occur, something he believes will prevent another fatal attack.

The father emphasized that accountability for October 7 should be prioritized as he believes this will assist in navigating other regional conflicts.

Some context: Chen’s son, Itay, had been serving with the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) on the Gaza border when he was killed. Initially, Itay was believed to have been abducted and held hostage by Hamas, but in March 2024, the IDF confirmed he had been killed on October 7. He was 19 years old.

Israelis woke up Wednesday to a familiar political deadlock, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition nor the opposition winning a clear majority to form a government.

These results build on the unprecedented streak of political paralysis that has produced six elections in seven years. Between 2019 and 2022, the country voted in five rounds of elections as no side could secure a clear 61-seat majority in the 120-seat parliament and sustain a viable coalition, reflecting a country deeply divided over leadership and direction.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest serving prime minister, is also the first sitting prime minister to be indicted for corruption charges. That has broadly shaped the country’s political map during his tenure, as most of the opposition parties have refused to work with him, pushing him deeper into a reliance on far-right and ultra-orthodox parties. Only in the 2022 election did he and his allies win a majority.

Relying on the support of nationalistic and religious parties, Netanyahu held his government together for its full four-years, the first time since 1988 a government had lasted its complete term.

Shortly after the government’s inauguration, it pushed for a sweeping judicial overhaul that was met with widespread liberal protests, that continued up until the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel, the greatest security failure in the country’s history, and a multi-front war that followed.

Once again, this vote was a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership, but also about the country’s direction and identity. The results reinforce the deep divide and polarization between Israelis over democratic values, religion and state, military service and accountability.

The left-wing Democrats Party – part of the opposition bloc – is saying what no other opposition party has been willing to say so far: to form a government, you must work with the Arab parties.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc is projected to take 54 seats; the opposition bloc – led by his main rival Gadi Eisenkot— now is expected to take 47 seats. But neither have enough seats to form a majority in the 120-member Israeli Knesset.

That’s where the Arab parties – who are set to hold a record 17 seats – come in.

Democrats leader Yair Golan on Wednesday urged the opposition bloc to work with them – not as a gesture, but because that is the simple political math required to form a government and oust Netanyahu.

“Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120,” he said.

Golan is urging other opposition leaders – who have expressed ideological opposition to working with the Arab parties – to overcome their divisions to secure a coalition.

“We have no future here if we don’t stop being afraid. And if we don’t stop with the racism. We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” he said.

Netanyahu has long disparaged the idea of a political partnership with Arab parties, despite reaching out to Mansour Abbas’ Raam party after the 2021 vote. The Arab population makes up 20% of Israel’s population, but Netanyahu has framed any such alliance as a threat.

Speaking on Israeli Army radio on Wednesday, Arab lawmaker Ahmad Tibi said that that “the change bloc can form a government – we are willing to help.”

“Netanyahu won’t be able to form a government,” Tibi said. “The other side can, if they want, if they have courage.”

The exit polls that flashed on Israeli televisions mark the beginning of a long counting process in which results can shift hours and sometimes days after the polls close. This is because of a voting system known as the double envelopes.

The vast majority of Israeli voters are assigned to specific polling stations - and their ballots are opened and counted the moment polls close. But a group of voters - soldiers, prisoners, hospital patients and staff, diplomats abroad and voters with disabilities - cast their ballot inside a double envelope.

These voters place their anonymous vote in an inner envelope, which is sealed inside an outer envelope with their personal details. The double envelopes are transported to the Central Elections Committee, where staff check each outer envelope against the registered polling stations to verify the voter didn’t vote twice. Only then are the inner envelopes separated and counted.

That verification process takes time. The Central Elections Committee said there are more double envelopes than ever this year. The committee is expecting as many as 650,000 Israelis to vote this way, up from 460,000 in the 2022 elections. The surge is attributed mainly to the large number of military reservists currently deployed and voting away from home. Together they could amount to a game-changing 15 seats that remain uncounted on election night.

The double envelopes historically change the map by 1-2 seats. Because of who votes like this, they tend to impact the ultra-Orthodox and Arab parties. For parties hovering around the 3.25% electoral threshold, they can be decisive.

Election night in Israel ends when all the votes are counted, but that is just the first step. Forming a government runs through the president of the state, who plays a pivotal role in post-election politics.

After the results are finalized, President Isaac Herzog will begin consultations with all the elected parties, asking each of them who they recommend to be prime minister. He then assigns the task of forming a government to the candidate he believes is most likely to secure a 61-seat majority. This is not necessarily the leader of the largest party, but the one he deems has a better path to a coalition.

When election results are clear, the choice can be obvious. If there is no clear winner or a deadlock, the president’s decision can be decisive for coalition negotiations.

After Herzog decides who gets the mandate, the assigned candidate will have 28 days - with a possible 14-day extension - to negotiate with other parties over cabinet posts, budget priorities and policy commitments.

The goal is simple: try to form a government. If that candidate fails, the mandate is passed to another candidate for another four weeks. If he fails as well, the Knesset gets a short window to put forward another candidate, and if it cannot then the country goes to another round of elections.

The current vote count shows neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his primary rival Gadi Eisenkot with a clear path to a majority, enhancing Herzog’s role in the process even more. With neither side holding a clear majority, he may try to steer the two largest parties to form a unity government. Two weeks before the election, Herzog said he will do everything he can “to establish a stable government” and avoid another election.

It’s 11 a.m. in Jerusalem and more than 70% of the vote has been counted. Here’s the current projections based on the ballots tallied so far:

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc is set to take 54 seats.

The opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, now has 47 seats.

Arab parties – Ra’am and the Joint List have 19 seats.

Despite there currently being no clear winner in the Israeli election, several players are claiming that preliminary results indicate success for both their parties and the country.

Here’s a look at what some of the key players are saying:

In a speech, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu touted a “decisive majority among the Zionist and Jewish public.” He thanked US President Donald Trump and God for making him Israel’s leader. “We made it against our enemies and we will form the future,” he said.

Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu’s main opponent, said that “the public has voted for change,” adding that Netanyahu’s “coalition of failure has lost the people’s trust.” Eisenkot said he would act with “all our power to establish a government,” and his party intends to represent all Israelis.

The Arab Joint List party , one of two major Arab parties, said in a statement: “We can say with confidence: we sent the fascist right-wing government to the dustbin of history.” Party leader Yousef Jabareen commended a strong turnout among the community, saying it was “unprecedented and historic in our Arab society.”

Mansour Abbas, the head of the other major Arab party Raam, said: “We will turn the seats we won into a new reality in the country.” He said that the “record-breaking electoral achievement” is because the current Israeli government “neglected the Israeli Arab community.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s principal opponent in the elections is a relative newcomer to politics. Instead, one of his key electoral advantages boils down to a simple truth: He is not Netanyahu.

Gadi Eisenkot, 66, has spent most of his life in the Israeli military, enlisting in the Golani Brigade in 1978 and rising over a 40-year career to become chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, serving under Netanyahu.

He entered politics in 2022 alongside another former chief of staff, Benny Gantz. After the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on Israel, the two joined Netanyahu’s emergency war cabinet. But they left in June 2024, pointing to the absence of a clear post-war strategy.

Eisenkot is the second of nine children and a father of five. His youngest son, Gal, 25, was killed fighting in Gaza two months into the war.

He has placed that singular promise at the heart of his political mission.

US President Donald Trump said early Wednesday he hadn’t yet spoken to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but seemed optimistic about his performance in the election as the vote count is underway.

Just over a week before the polls opened in Israel, Trump called Netanyahu a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” in a Truth Social post, offering his “Complete and Total Endorsement.”

Exit polls so far suggest Netanyahu’s bloc lost its majority in the Knesset — though it is narrowly in the lead over the opposition. Trump suggested that the exit polls might be wrong, however.

“He might be winning, or tied,” he said. “It’s a little bit early, but I’m hearing that in Israel, top people are saying, ‘Wow,’ he did a lot better than people thought.”

The final result could be “a stalemate or a win – but we’ll find out,” he added.

Supporters of Israel’s Arab Joint List party celebrated at its election headquarters in Nazareth, with Arab parties projected to gain a record number of seats from Tuesday’s election.

Party leader Yousef Jabareen commended a strong turnout among the community, saying it was “unprecedented and historic in our Arab society.” Arab voters make up about 20% of the Israeli electorate, but have traditionally voted at lower rates than Jewish Israelis.

That voter surge was driven by an urgent desire to dismantle Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition, which includes hardline ministers such as Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.

That sentiment was underscored by chants of “Ben-Gvir, go home” at the Joint List election headquarters.

Jabareen said exit polls showed Arab-led parties can “make a difference.”

He vowed to be a “safety net in the face of crime in our society, a safety net in the face of dangerous racism, a safety net in the face of the demolition of homes and entire villages.”

Some context: Entering government could still be tricky for Arab parties. Between them, the Joint List and Raam are projected to secure 17-19 seats in the 120-seat Knessett, their strongest showing in history.

Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party is projected to win 21-23 seats.

However, Eisenkot has set conditions for any partner to join his government, including recognizing Israel as a Jewish state and recognizing Hamas as a terrorist organization that must be dismantled, terms most Arab lawmakers are unlikely to accept.

Moreover, two of his opposition allies – Avigdor Lieberman and Naftali Bennett – have ruled out forming a government with the Arab parties altogether.

CNN’s Abeer Salman and Kara Fox contributed reporting.

It’s now Wednesday morning in Israel, and the election – one of the most consequential in years – is over. Next begins the real work of counting votes and forming a government.

It’ll take several days to finalize the vote count, but exit polls indicate Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party has taken a blow – though there’s not yet a clear winner with an outright majority.

Israel’s elections produced no clear winner Tuesday night, exit polls showed, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival Gadi Eisenkot within reach of the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat parliament, the Knesset. CNN's Jeremy Diamond reports.

Netanyahu stumbles: Netanyahu’s bloc of ultra-Orthodox and far-right allies has lost its majority. Projections from the Central Election Committee see Netanyahu’s party collapsing from 68 seats in the Knesset to 56. His Likud party will likely still be the largest single party, but the results represent a crash in public support.

‘Decisive majority’: Speaking in Jerusalem early Wednesday, Netanyahu said the results still showed his bloc had the support of a “decisive majority among the Zionist and Jewish public,” despite the loss in seats. He slammed Arab parties as “anti-Zionist” and rejected the idea of working with them to form a government. He also thanked US President Donald Trump for his support in the war with Iran.

Opposition bloc: Netanyahu’s biggest rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is narrowly behind, with his bloc projected to secure 48 seats. “The public has voted for change,” he said. But he doesn’t have a clear path to a governing majority yet, either.

Arab parties surge: Arab parties Joint List and Raam are projected to win a record 19 seats – the largest Arab representation ever. They could play a key role in building a coalition to form a new government. But what that could look like remains unclear.

Record turnout: Nearly 5.7 million voters cast their ballot out of approximately 7.3 million eligible voters – meaning a turnout of 77.7%, the highest percentage since 1999, according to the Central Elections Committee.

What’s next: Once the votes are finalized, each elected party will recommend their choice for prime minister to the president, who will select one person to try to form a government – based on who has the best chance of building a viable coalition. The way things look now, that will likely be Eisenkot, who will have four to six weeks to negotiate with other parties and try to cobble together a majority in the Knesset. But he could also fail, and Netanyahu could be given a chance to try. If he fails too, and if the Knesset cannot put forth another candidate, Israel could hold elections all over again.

Why this matters: This election has been widely viewed as a referendum on Netanyahu, and whether Israel keeps moving in the nationalistic, conservative and religious direction – or changes course. For many voters, this is the first chance to pass judgment on the leadership that presided over October 7 failures, and to decide who should lead the country in conflict.

articles.title: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.summary: Scores of people have been killed and around 100 injured after two Spanish trains — carrying about 500 passengers — collided south of Madrid. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• Deadly rail crash: Scores of people have been killed and about 100 injured after a high-speed train collided with a stationary train. Spain’s transport minister called it “inexplicable” that a train was allowed to continue its journey despite a red signal being in place.

• ‘People were hurled into the air ’: Several witnesses told CNN about the chaotic moment when passengers were thrown airborne during the collision. Rescue operations are still under and the high-speed line linking Madrid with Andalusia remains suspended.

• Third train crash this year: This is the third rail disaster in Spain in 2026. In January, two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz , in southern Spain’s Córdoba province, killing more than 40 people. A commuter train near Barcelona derailed days later.

“Several” US citizens were injured in the train crash in Spain, a US State Department spokesperson told CNN.

They did not provide specific details on the number of Americans hurt in Wednesday’s deadly train crash, which has killed at least 68 people.

“The Department of State and the US Embassy in Madrid are working closely with local authorities to assist Americans following the train collision,” the spokesperson said. “We extend our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of all those affected.”

CNN saw US embassy officials at the scene of the collision in Spain’s Toledo province.

The spokesperson noted that Americans in need of consular assistance, or with concerns about American loved ones in Spain, can contact the State Department 24/7 at +1-202-501-4444 from abroad or +1-888-407-4747 from the US and Canada.

“We encourage US citizens in the area to notify loved ones of their safety and monitor local media for updates,” they said.

Spain’s King Felipe VI has conveyed his condolences over today’s deadly train crash in the Spanish province of Toledo, saying he shares in the “sorrow of the families and loved ones” of the deceased.

The social media post said the royal family’s support goes out to the emergency teams involved in the recovery effort and “all those working in the area to help as much as possible under these circumstances.”

CNN’s Duarte Mendonca contributed reporting.

After a host of European leaders offered their condolences for the victims of the deadly train crash in Spain this morning, other international leaders are also expressing their solidarity today.

Cuba’s Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla sent his country’s “deepest condolences” to the people of Spain, “especially to the families and loved ones of the victims.”

Uruguay ’s Foreign Ministry sent its “deepest condolences to the families of the victims, to the Government and the Spanish people.”

Jordan’s Foreign Ministry expressed “solidarity and full support with the government and people of Spain,” offering “condolences to the families of the victims and wishing a speedy recovery to the injured.”

The Palestinian Authority in Ramallah also said it extends “its warmest condolences and sincere sympathy to the families” of those affected by the collision.

Egypt’s Foreign Ministry expressed “solidarity” toward Spain’s “painful affliction” after the incident.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said he is “profoundly grieved by the devastating train collision,” sending his condolences to those affected by it. “Pakistan stands with Spain in its hour of sorrow,” he said .

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar offered his country’s “solidarity and most sincere condolences” to those affected. “In these difficult times we join the sorrow of the Spanish,” he said.

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan offered “solidarity with the victim’s families and a quick recovery for the injured” in a post on X. “Armenia shares your pain and wishes you strength,” he said.

An erroneous order from a train controller, following a signaling system failure, resulted in Wednesday’s deadly train crash, according to Spain’s transport minister.

Speaking during a press conference on Wednesday afternoon, Óscar Puente said that a computer failure with the main LZB signalling system triggered an automatic stop for all trains in that area, including the Renfe high-speed train and Iryo train involved in the collision.

The control system for Adif, Spain’s railway infrastructure manager, then took command of the system and a decision was made for the Renfe train to continue its journey and the train was authorized to proceed despite a red signal prohibiting movement remaining in place.

The Iryo train remained stationary on the track around 25 kilometers (16 miles) ahead.

The Renfe train was authorized to proceed without any speed restrictions, meaning that between 8:36 a.m. and 8:52 a.m. local time, it traveled approximately 25 kilometers (16 miles) at a speed of about 200 kilometers per hour (124 miles per hour) before colliding with the Iryo train, Puente said.

The transport minister described the crash as “truly implausible” and said that the control center’s decision to allow the Renfe train to resume its journey while the Iryo train was stopped on the track was “inexplicable.”

This post has been updated with additional reporting.

Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said authorities are working hard to identify the cause of today’s deadly train crash in Toledo province, and vowed that any negligence, if identified, will be addressed with “utmost firmness.”

Sánchez added that if Spain must “strengthen safety even further in order to rebuild confidence in our high-speed rail system, we will do so. Because what is unacceptable for a country like Spain is to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year, as we have.”

“Therefore, every measure considered appropriate will be taken,” he said.

He also said the cause of the crash was “not for me to say,” but rather for the train network operators and the country’s Independent Commission on Rail Accidents to investigate.

Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is at the scene of the train collision, where he offered his condolences and announced three days of official mourning.

“Today, Spain is in mourning. All of Spain is in mourning,” he said, saying he expressed his “full solidarity” with victims’ families.

“Behind every person who has died today, there are shattered lives, there are broken families. There is also the anguish of those families who still do not know the whereabouts of their loved ones. And, of course, there is a great deal of pain, a great deal of pain that Spanish society as a whole naturally shares.”

At least 68 people have been killed and another 58 have been injured after two trains collided in the Spanish province of Toledo, local officials have said.

Here are some of the latest developments:

Human error may have played a part in the deadly crash , Spanish media has suggested, suggesting that a railway controller could have made a mistake that led to the collision.

A woman traveling on one of the trains involved in the deadly collision has described “awful” scenes as people were thrown into the air.

Several passengers were seen by a CNN team with minor injuries, including cuts on their faces and around their eyes, and what appeared to be bloody noses. Many people also had blood on their hands and arms.

The scene at the site of the crash is frantic as a serious rescue operation is underway, with dozens of fire trucks, ambulances and police cars present, according to CNN’s team on the ground in Toledo province.

The Spanish Civil Guard has opened four offices in different cities of Spain in order to swiftly identify the victims of the crash.

Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will travel to Urda , the town closest to the site of the collision, the country’s government said on X.

European leaders have been quick to share their condolences , with Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro offering his country’s “availability for whatever may be necessary” following the collision.

CNN’s Magdalena Sofia Vitores Moreno, Benjamin Brown, Sophie Tanno, Vasco Cotovio, Pau Mosquera and Lauren Kent contributed to this reporting.

Emergency crews are working at the site of a deadly train collision in Spain’s Toledo province today, in which at least 64 people were killed and dozens more injured.

Train passengers have told CNN that the moment of the crash was “very chaotic” and people were immediately thrown out of their seats and on top of one another inside the train carriages.

Authorities have moved at least one bus full of passengers who do not have serious injuries away from the site. Several passengers being bussed away had minor injuries, including cuts on their faces and around their eyes, and what appeared to be bloody noses. Many people also had blood on their hands and arms.

“There was terrible communication. No one could leave the trains for 10 minutes after the crash, we didn’t know what was happening,” said one passenger, Rey, who declined to give his last name.

He said he and his family, who were on the way to a vacation in Seville, are OK but also “desperate to go.” More busses have arrived on the scene now to move additional passengers away from the area.

Another passenger, Yoander, 25, told CNN: “I was sleeping, and when I woke up I was already crashing into the seats in front of me.”

“I hit my face and my leg,” he said. “I’m in pain, but there are people that need more help than I do.”

The deadly train crash in Spain’s Toledo province has some similarities with a train disaster in Córdoba province that killed more than 40 people earlier this year.

Both train collisions happened along the same high-speed rail route that runs between the capital, Madrid, and Seville, about 300 miles south.

The Toledo crash happened about 130 miles from the site of January’s train disaster near Adamuz , in Córdoba province. Following Wednesday’s crash, authorities have suspended that high-speed line linking the Madrid region with Andalusia.

Both train accidents also involved the collision of two high-speed trains, although one of the trains on Wednesday was not travelling at high speed at the time of the crash.

Spanish emergency authorities have not yet announced a precise cause of Wednesday’s crash, but they have disclosed some details. The local Castilla-La Mancha 112 emergency services told CNN they received a report of a collision at 8.45 a.m. local time. According to the reports, a train owned by the company Iryo was stationary or traveling at low speed when it was struck by a high-speed AVE train operated by Spain’s national railway company Renfe.

It appears the crash on Wednesday was a rear-end collision, authorities at the scene told CNN. The train crash earlier this year involved one train derailing and crossing onto an adjacent track, according to Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE.

For context: Spain’s train drivers’ union, Semaf, has previously raised concerns about high speeds causing vibrations and subsequent wear and tear along high-speed railway lines, a source from the union told CNN in January, in the aftermath of the crash near Adamuz.

In August 2025, the union sent a letter to the national railway operator, Adif, asking for a reduction in the maximum speed on all high-speed train lines from 300 kmph to 250 kmph, after some stretches were vibrating and placing stress on the infrastructure, the source said.

CNN’s Pau Mosquera, Tim Lister and Sophie Tanno contributed to this report.

Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will travel to Urda, the town closest to the site of the train crash, the country’s government said in a post on X.

While in Urda, Sanchez will “back the works of the emergency teams and bring support to the affected and their families,” the government said.

There has been an outpouring of grief from neighboring European leaders today, after two trains collided in the Spanish province of Toledo, killing dozens of people.

Portugal ’s Prime Minister Luís Montenegro expressed his “condolences and profound solidarity” to those affected, offering his country’s “availability for whatever may be necessary” following the collision.

Italy’ s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said he was following developments “with deep concern,” adding that the Italian Consulate General in Madrid was working to verify possible involvement of Italian citizens in the crash.

French President Emmanuel Macron offered his country’s thoughts to the victims of the collision and their families, as well as emergency crews working on the scene. “To the Spanish people, I express the solidarity of France,” he said.

Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, called the news of the collision “devastating” and said that her “heart goes out to the victims’ families and loved ones.” In a post on X , von der Leyen said: “Today, Europe mourns with you.”

Meanwhile, Benjamín León Jr, the US Spain’s state-owned public broadcaster to Spain, said he was “closely following” the news of the crash “with deep concern.” Offering his thoughts to the victims, León Jr said that “all our support is with the emergency services that are working on the grounds now. We are with Spain in these moments.”

CNN’s James Frater, Duarte Mendonça, Sharon Braithwaite and Magdalena Vitores Moreno contributed to this reporting.

Correction : An earlier version of this post misstated the title of French President Emmanuel Macron.

At least 64 people have now been confirmed killed in a deadly train collision in Spain this morning, a spokesperson for the regional Castilla-La Mancha government said.

The spokesperson told CNN that this number is expected to rise further as emergency workers continue to work at the scene.

The death toll from today’s train crash in the Spanish province of Toledo has now risen to at least 32, according to Emiliano García-Page, the president of the regional Castilla-La Mancha government.

García-Page shared the latest update when speaking to Spanish national broadcaster Radio Nacional de España.

Previously, authorities had said that at least 30 people had been killed and around 100 injured in the collision.

The Spanish Civil Guard announced that they have opened four offices in different cities of Spain in order to swiftly identify the victims of the crash.

A spokesperson of institution has said they will also take DNA samples of the relatives to bring a quick response. “We are calling all close relatives to get to this offices and speed up the identification process,” the spokesperson said.

The offices are in the Civil Guard zones of Madrid, Andalusia, Cordoba and Toledo.

CNN’s Pau Mosquera has been reporting from Urda, a town roughly five miles from the site of today’s deadly train crash.

Dozens of ambulances and emergency service vehicles have been streaming into the town’s sports centre, where Red Cross workers are treating the injured.

One of the survivors recounted how she was thrown from her seat as the crash’s impact sent her flying into the air. She was grateful for the care provided to her by the emergency staff in Urda.

The scene at the site of the crash is frantic as a serious rescue operation is underway, according to CNN’s team on the ground in Toledo province.

Dozens of fire trucks, ambulances and police cars are here. At least three helicopters are also at the crash site to assist with operations. Multiple ambulances have come and gone from the cordoned-off area.

Meanwhile, emergency responders are combing through the rubble of some of the heavily damaged carriages of the train operated by Iryo. Several carriages of the state-owned Renfe high-speed train are tilted on their side after coming off the rails.

The Spanish civil guard has set up multiple tents for what amounts to a huge emergency response.

Authorities have moved a bus full of passengers who do not have serious injuries away from the site, and some those passengers told CNN they are now being taken to their original destination of Sevilla.

Passengers described a chaotic scene when their train hit another train on the tracks.

Those being bussed away from the crash site included citizens of multiple nationalities, including Spain, Brazil and elsewhere. Staff from the US Embassy in Spain are also at the site.

A woman traveling on one of the trains involved in a deadly collision Wednesday morning has described “awful” scenes as people were thrown into the air.

Patricia was sitting in the third carriage of the AVE high speed train, operated by Renfe, Spain’s national railway company, when it collided with a train owned by the company Iryo.

Speaking to CNN, Patricia told how her train had been stopped for around 20 minutes before the accident, with an announcement explaining there was a lot of traffic. “After that we departed, and maybe not after even three minutes, there was a crash,” she said.

Patricia said the crash seemed to last a long time.

The Castilla-La Mancha regional government has called for blood donations following today’s train crash.

“Donate blood,” reads a post on X. “Today your solidarity is very important.”

The post calls for donations in Alcázar de San Juan, Ciudad Real and Toledo.

At least 30 people have been killed and around a hundred injured in a collision between two trains in the Spanish province of Toledo this morning, according to a local government official and emergency services. The incident is the third rail disaster in Spain this year.

Here’s what we know about the deadly collision so far :

The first reports of a collision were received around 8:45 a.m. local time (3:45 a.m. ET), a regional Emergency Services spokesperson told CNN.

According to the reports, one train, managed by the company Iryo, was either stopped or moving at a low speed when it was struck by the other train, operated by the company Renfe. Part of the Renfe train left the tracks, while several carriages of the Iryo train derailed.

There were 146 passengers and a baby traveling on one train and 397 passengers on the other, Esther Padilla, the spokesperson of the regional government Castilla and La Mancha, said.

Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he was “shocked by the serious train incident,” adding that emergency services were on the ground to assist those impacted in the crash.

Football teams, including LaLiga giants Real Madrid and FC Barcelona, have issued statements of condolences following the deadly collision.

CNN’s Pau Mosquera, Sophie Tanno, Magdalena Sofia Vitores Moreno and Lauren Kent contributed to this reporting.
